headline: Kalyn Ponga Guides New Zealand To Rugby League World Cup Final
seoTitle: Ponga Leads Kiwis To Rugby League World Cup Final
metaDescription: Kalyn Ponga has returned from a broken arm to lead New Zealand into their first Rugby League World Cup final since 2013 following a semifinal victory.
aiSummaryBullets: Kalyn Ponga made an immediate return to professional rugby league after being sidelined for 23 days with a fractured arm.
The New Zealand squad secured a spot in the Rugby League World Cup final following a victory in their recent semifinal match.
This appearance marks the first time the national team has reached the championship match of the tournament since 2013.
aiContextParagraph: The New Zealand rugby league team has officially qualified for the upcoming Rugby League World Cup final. The team's path to the championship stage was anchored by the performance of Kalyn Ponga, who rejoined the squad after a three-week recovery period from a broken arm. His return to the lineup coincided with a significant semifinal win, marking a notable milestone for the national program as they prepare for the tournament's conclusion. This victory represents the first time New Zealand has reached the final round of the competition since 2013, when they previously contested the title. The match also drew attention for pre-match rituals performed by the players before the game began. The team now looks ahead to the final fixture as they aim for their first tournament win in over a decade, with Ponga expected to play a central role after his swift return to active competition.
